XI.}}</noinclude>{{dropinitial|A|fl={{verse|chapter=11|verse=1}}}}ND it came to passe, vvhen he was in a certaine place, praying, as he ceased, one of his Disciples said to him, Lord teach vs to pray, as Iohn also taught his Disciples. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=2}}† And he said to them, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 6, 9.''}}* VVhen you pray, say, ''{{sc|Father}}, sanctified be thy name. Thy kingdom come'', {{verse|chapter=11|verse=3}}† ''Our daily bread giue vs this day'', {{verse|chapter=11|verse=4}}† ''and forgiue vs our sinnes, for because our selues also doe forgiue euery one that is in debt to vs. And lead vs not into temptation''. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=5}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel in ''Maioribus Litanijs'' on S. Markes day, and in the Rogation daies. And in a votiue Masse against the Pagans.}}And he said to them, VVhich of you shal haue a frende, and shal goe to him at midnight, and shal say to him, Frende, lend me three loaues, {{verse|chapter=11|verse=6}}† because a frende of mine is come out of his way to me, and I haue not what to set before him: {{verse|chapter=11|verse=7}}† & he from vvithin ansvvering saith, Trouble me not, novv the doore is shut, and my children are vvith me in bed: I can not rise and giue thee. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=8}}† And if he shal perseuêre knocking, I say to you, although he vvil not rise and giue him because he is his frende, yet for his importunitie he vvil rise, and giue him as many as he needeth. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=9}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 7, 7.''}}* {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel in a votiue Masse for sinnes.}}And I say to you, Aske, and it shal be giuen you: seeke, and you shal finde: knocke, and it shal be opened to you. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=10}}† For euery one that asketh, receiueth: and he that seeketh, findeth: and to him that knocketh, it shal be opened. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=11}}† And vvhich of you if he aske his father bread, vvil he giue him a stone? or a fish, vvil he for a fish giue him a serpent? {{verse|chapter=11|verse=12}}† Or if he aske an egge, vvil he reach him a scorpion? {{verse|chapter=11|verse=13}}† If you then being naught, knovv hovv to giue good giftes to your children, hovv much more vvil your father from heauen giue the good spirit to them that aske him?⊣

{{verse|chapter=11|verse=14}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 12, 22.''}}* And he vvas casting out a deuil, and that vvas dumme. And vvhen he had cast out the deuil, the dumme spake: and the multitudes marueiled. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=15}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mr. 3, 22.''}}* {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Mt. 12, 22. · The Gospel vpō the 3 Sunday in Lent.}}∷ And certaine of them said, In Beel-zebub the prince of Deuils he casteth out Deuils. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=16}}† And other tempting, asked of him a signe from heauen. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=17}}† But he seeing their cogitations, said to them, Euery kingdom deuided against it self, shal be made desolate, and c {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''ὀῖκος ἐπὶ ὀῖκον''}}∷ house vpon house, shal fall. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=18}}† And if Satan also be deuided against him self, hovv shal his kingdom stand? because you say that in Beel-zebub I doe cast out Deuils. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=19}}† And if I in Beel-zebub cast out Deuils: your children, in vvhom doe they cast out? therfore they shal be your iudges. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=20}}† But if I in the {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ This finger, is the spirit of God, ''Mt. 12, 28''.}}∷ finger of<noinclude>{{rh|||God}}</noinclude>
